newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of East Asia may issue LAF FRCD.
newsitem.headline: Bank of East Asia may issue LAF FRCD.

text.p: The Bank of East Asia may make a floating rate certificates of deposit issue before the end of the year, market sources said.
They said the proposed issue would be HK$1.8 billion in size and carry a tenor of three years.
The sources said they expected the bank will apply to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
The Bank of East Asia is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service.
Sources said the bank was close to mandating a group of banks to arrange the issue.
Company officials could not be reached for comment.

In February, the bank completed a HK$2 billion three-year LAF floating rate certificates of deposit issue that paid a margin of 40 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the issue paid an all-in return of 48 basis points.
